mixed3a:110.CP_s1: The unit responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform surface on the left meets a fine, repeating dotted or granular texture on the right. Examples include knit stitches, perforated grilles, polka dots, keypads, thatch and leopard print.
mixed3a:110.CP_s2: The unit responds to a vertical boundary with a smooth, uniform surface on the left and a dense texture of small repeated dots or blobs on the right (knit stitches, speaker holes, polka dots, keypad buttons, QR code, thatch, leopard print).
mixed3a:110.CP_s3: Responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a dense, fine repeating texture (dots, holes, knit, perforations, spotted patterns) on the right.
mixed3a:110.CPS_s1: Responds to a vertical boundary where a plain, smooth region on the left meets a dense dotted or granular texture on the right (a textured object's left edge), with the texture occupying the right half of the receptive field.
mixed3a:110.CPS_s2: Responds to a vertical boundary with a smooth, uniform region on the left and a dense, fine dotted or bumpy texture (knit, perforations, polka dots, sequins, buttons) on the right.
mixed3a:110.CPS_s3: Responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform surface on the left meets a dense dotted or granular texture on the right, such as polka dots, perforations, knit, beads or keypad buttons.
mixed3a:110.CPN_s1: The unit responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a dense repeating texture of small dots, spots, or knit-like blobs on the right (polka dots, perforations, keypads, sequins, thatch, scales).
mixed3a:110.CPN_s2: The unit responds to a vertical boundary where a smooth, plain region on the left meets a fine dotted, beaded or granular texture on the right (knit, perforations, polka dots, keypad buttons, thatch, grains).
mixed3a:110.CPN_s3: The unit fires on a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine, dense dotted or speckled texture on the right, such as knit stitches, grille holes, polka dots, keypad buttons, a QR code or sequins.
mixed3a:110.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to a vertical border with a smooth, uniform surface on the left and a fine dotted, knobbly or granular texture on the right, such as a knit, polka dots, perforations, keypad buttons or thatch.
mixed3a:110.CPSN_s2: The unit responds to a vertical boundary with a smooth, plain surface on the left and a fine repeating dot or granular texture on the right, such as perforations, polka dots, knit or beading.
mixed3a:110.CPSN_s3: The unit fires at a vertical boundary where a smooth, uniform region on the left meets a fine dotted or speckled texture on the right, such as knit, perforations, polka dots or keypad buttons.

mixed3b:379.CP_s1: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular object, i.e. a convex arc boundary, usually with a concentric band or ring inside it; it fires most strongly on watch, compass and gauge dials and more weakly on other arcs such as bridge arches, bowl rims and curved railings.
mixed3b:379.CP_s2: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular object, mostly the bezel or edge of a round dial (watch, compass, gauge, clock face, plaque), seen as a convex arc with concentric bands or a thin border. It also responds more weakly to other curved arcs such as a bridge arch, a bowl rim, rainbow-like stripes and a bent railing.
mixed3b:379.CP_s3: The unit responds to the curved upper edge of a circular rim or dial, a convex arc bordering a round face, mostly on watches, compasses, gauges and clock faces. It responds more weakly to other arched contours such as bridge arches, bowl rims, rainbow stripes and curved railings.
mixed3b:379.CPS_s1: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular object, mostly the bezels and dial edges of watches, compasses, clocks and gauges, where a curved band contour sits against a contrasting background. It also responds more weakly to other arcs, such as a bowl rim, a bridge arch, a plaque edge and a curved railing.
mixed3b:379.CPS_s2: The unit detects the curved upper rim of a circular object, an arc that bulges upward where a ring or bezel meets its interior. It responds most to watch, compass and gauge dials, and more weakly to any upward-curved arc such as a bridge arch, a bowl rim, a rainbow logo or a bent railing.
mixed3b:379.CPS_s3: The unit detects curved circular rims or arcs, usually the upper edge of a round dial-like object such as a watch face, compass, gauge or round plaque, where a band or bezel follows the curve. Weaker responses come from other arcs such as a bridge arch, a bowl rim, a rainbow-like stripe sign and a curved railing.
mixed3b:379.CPN_s1: The unit detects the curved upper-left rim of a circular object, chiefly the bezel or edge of a round dial on watches, compasses, gauges and clocks. It also fires more weakly on other circular arcs such as plaques, bowl rims, bridge arches and curved railings.
mixed3b:379.CPN_s2: The unit detects the curved upper rim or bezel of a circular dial or disc: the arc where a round face such as a watch, compass, gauge or clock meets its border, typically with tick marks or text just inside it. It responds more weakly to other round arcs, such as a bowl rim, a bridge arch, a plaque edge or a bent rail.
mixed3b:379.CPN_s3: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular object, usually the bezel and edge of a round dial such as a watch, compass, gauge or clock, with markings or ticks along the inside of the arc. It also responds more weakly to other circular arcs like bowl rims, plaque edges, a bridge arch and a bent railing.
mixed3b:379.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to the curved upper rim of a round, dial-like object, the arc where a circular bezel or frame meets the dial face inside it. It fires most for watch, compass, gauge and clock faces, and more weakly for other circular arcs such as bowl rims, bridge arches, plaques and rainbow-like stripes.
mixed3b:379.CPSN_s2: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular dial or disc, the arc where a round bezel meets its face, as on watches, compasses, gauges and clocks. It responds more weakly to other convex arcs such as bridge arches, bowl rims, signs and handrails.
mixed3b:379.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to the curved upper-left rim of a circular dial or disc, where a ring or bezel meets the face, as on watches, compasses, gauges and clock faces. It responds more weakly to other curved arcs such as plaques, bowls, a bridge arch and railings.

mixed4b:237.CP_s1: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles: the glass panes in a vehicle door and their frames, mostly the front cab or door window of cars, pickups, vans and trucks seen from the side.
mixed4b:237.CP_s2: Responds to the side window and door region of road vehicles (cars, trucks, vans, ambulances), i.e. the window frame/pillar area of a vehicle cab seen from the side or front three-quarters.
mixed4b:237.CP_s3: Responds to the side door-window region of road vehicles (cars, trucks, vans, cabs), meaning the framed side window with its pillar and door edge seen in roughly upright side or three-quarter view.
mixed4b:237.CPS_s1: Responds to the side windows of road vehicles, especially the front side window, door and A-pillar region of cars, trucks, vans and ambulances. Weaker responses extend to similar rectangular framed glass or panels such as train door windows, boat cabins and windowed screen icons.
mixed4b:237.CPS_s2: The unit responds to the side windows and door frames of road vehicles (cars, pickups, vans, trucks), especially the framed window area on the vehicle's side. It responds more weakly to other framed rectangular panels such as train doors, boat cabins and screen icons.
mixed4b:237.CPS_s3: Responds to the side window and door of road vehicles, meaning the cab or cabin window framed by the door pillar and the edge of the roof, in cars, trucks, vans and ambulances. It responds more weakly to similar framed rectangular windows or panels elsewhere, such as train doors, boats and slot-machine buttons.
mixed4b:237.CPN_s1: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles: the glass pane of a car, truck or van door, framed by the door pillar and window frame, usually in its upright orientation.
mixed4b:237.CPN_s2: Responds to the side windows and door region of a vehicle cab, where the window frame meets the door panel, on cars, trucks, vans and emergency vehicles.
mixed4b:237.CPN_s3: The unit responds to the side windows of road vehicles, specifically the upright window and door-frame area of a car or truck cab (the side glass with its pillars and frame), seen from the side in its normal upright orientation.
mixed4b:237.CPSN_s1: Responds to the side windows of road vehicles, meaning the glass pane, its frame, door edge and mirror on the cab or passenger door of cars, trucks, vans and ambulances. It responds weakly to other upright framed glossy rectangular panels such as slot-machine buttons, train door windows and boat cabins.
mixed4b:237.CPSN_s2: The unit detects the side windows of road vehicles, especially the front side window of the cab with its door frame and pillars, on cars, pickups, vans and trucks. It responds more weakly to other framed window- or panel-like shapes, such as train doors, boat cabins and screen icons.
mixed4b:237.CPSN_s3: Responds to the side window and door of a road vehicle, meaning the upper door panel with its window frame and side mirror on cars, pickups, vans and emergency trucks. It responds weakly to similar framed rectangular panels on other objects, such as train doors, boat cabins and screen icons.

mixed4b:373.CP_s1: The unit responds to vehicle wheels seen from the side together with the curved wheel arch or fender around them, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines, in their usual upright orientation.
mixed4b:373.CP_s2: The unit detects a vehicle wheel sitting under its wheel arch: a round tire/hub inside the curved fender opening, seen from the side and upright.
mixed4b:373.CP_s3: The unit responds to the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side, meaning the tire together with the curved wheel arch or fender above it, on cars, vans, buses and trucks alike.
mixed4b:373.CPS_s1: The unit detects the front wheel of a road vehicle, meaning the tyre and hub framed by the arch of the wheel well, seen from the side and upright. It responds weakly to other upright round or arched shapes such as bicycle wheels, tractor wheels and round metal objects.
mixed4b:373.CPS_s2: Responds to the wheel of a road vehicle sitting in its wheel arch, i.e. the tire/rim together with the curved fender edge above it, seen upright from the side or at a three-quarter angle.
mixed4b:373.CPS_s3: The unit detects a road-vehicle wheel seen in side view together with the arched wheel well or fender above it, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines. It responds weakly to other circular rims or bosses, such as bicycle and tractor wheels, coins and ornate circular metalwork.
mixed4b:373.CPN_s1: The unit detects the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side: a round tyre and hub sitting under the curved wheel-arch cutout of the body panel.
mixed4b:373.CPN_s2: The unit detects the wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side, together with the arched wheel well and fender over it, in an upright orientation.
mixed4b:373.CPN_s3: The unit detects a vehicle wheel seen from the side, together with the curved wheel-arch/fender around it, on cars, vans, buses, trucks and fire engines.
mixed4b:373.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to the wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side, specifically the tire together with the curved wheel arch above it (the front wheel of cars, vans, trucks, buses and fire engines). It responds weakly to other upright circular or arched shapes such as bicycle and tractor wheels and round metal rims.
mixed4b:373.CPSN_s2: The unit responds to the front wheel of a road vehicle seen from the side: a tyre inside its wheel arch on the lower body of cars, vans, trucks, buses and fire engines. It responds more weakly to other round wheel-like or circular rim shapes, such as bicycle wheels, tractor tyres, and circular metal reliefs.
mixed4b:373.CPSN_s3: Responds to a vehicle's wheel seen from the side together with the curved wheel arch/fender above it, most strongly the front wheel of cars, trucks, buses and emergency vehicles.

mixed4b:431.CP_s1: The unit responds to furry mammal heads and bodies, mainly dogs, at the fur region beside the face (cheek, ear, neck). It responds more weakly to other furry mammals with similar fur-around-face structure, such as monkeys, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink.
mixed4b:431.CP_s2: The unit responds to furry mammal heads and upper bodies, mostly dogs, with the box usually landing on fur at the side of the head, the ear or the neck/shoulder near the face. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar head and fur structure (dhole, hyena, monkeys, hamster, squirrel, mink).
mixed4b:431.CP_s3: Responds to furry mammal heads and fore-bodies, mostly dogs, typically at the fur near the side of the head, ear or neck. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as primates, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink.
mixed4b:431.CPS_s1: The unit responds to the side of the head and neck of furry mammals, mainly dogs, at the cheek, ear or neck region, often seen in left-facing or three-quarter view. It responds more weakly to the same region on other furry animals such as monkeys, hyenas, hamsters, squirrels and mink, and to human head and shoulder regions.
mixed4b:431.CPS_s2: Responds to the furry side of an animal's head or neck, such as the cheek, ear or neck fur of a mostly front-facing mammal (dogs especially). It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as monkeys, a hyena, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink, and to similar head-side regions like a person's or bird's.
mixed4b:431.CPS_s3: The unit responds to furry mammal heads seen in a particular orientation, mostly the fur on the side of the head, cheek or ear region of dogs facing right. It extends weakly to other furry mammals such as primates, hyena, hamster, squirrel and mink.
mixed4b:431.CPN_s1: The unit responds to furry mammal heads and faces, mostly dogs, firing on the furred head, ear and cheek region of large, close, roughly upright animals. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals such as dhole, hyena, monkeys, hamster, squirrel and mink.
mixed4b:431.CPN_s2: Responds to furry mammal heads and upper bodies seen close up and upright, mostly dogs, peaking on the fur near the face, ears and neck/shoulder. It extends more weakly to other furry mammals with similar faces (dhole, hyena, monkeys, hamster, squirrel, mink).
mixed4b:431.CPN_s3: Responds to the furry head-and-neck/shoulder region of mammals seen at close-to-medium range, mostly dogs, peaking on fur near the face, ears, cheek or neck, with weaker extensions to dog-like or furry mammals (dhole, hyena, proboscis and capuchin monkeys, hamster, squirrel, mink).
mixed4b:431.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to furry mammal heads and upper bodies, mostly dogs, firing on fur near the side of the face, the ear, cheek or neck. It is weaker on other furry mammals such as monkeys, hyenas, hamsters, squirrels and mink.
mixed4b:431.CPSN_s2: The unit responds to furry mammal fur at the side of an upright animal's head, neck or shoulder, mostly in dogs and dog-like animals (dhole, hyena). It also fires more weakly on other furry mammals such as monkeys, a hamster, a squirrel and a mink.
mixed4b:431.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to furry fur on the side or back of a mammal's head, such as the cheek, ear or neck. It fires most for dogs and wild canids, and more weakly for other furry mammals like monkeys, hamsters, squirrels, hyenas and mink. It seems to prefer one left-right layout, where the fur sits to the left of a face that extends to the right.

mixed4b:443.CP_s1: The unit detects upright canine faces, most strongly the eye/upper-face region of dogs, and extends more weakly to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.CP_s2: Responds to upright canine faces, peaking around the eye/upper-face region of dogs, and weakly extends to closely related canids such as wolves and foxes (#4, #9, #16).
mixed4b:443.CP_s3: Responds to the eye/upper-face region of upright, frontal dog faces (eye, brow and muzzle-bridge configuration), and extends more weakly to closely related canids such as foxes and wolves.
mixed4b:443.CPS_s1: The unit responds to upright canine faces, firing most on the eye region of dogs, wolves and foxes seen from the front. It gives weaker responses to other upright furry mammal faces (red panda, bear) and very weak ones to human or bird faces.
mixed4b:443.CPS_s2: The unit responds to upright, front-facing canid faces (dogs, wolves, foxes), peaking around the eye region between the eye and the ear or forehead. It also responds more weakly to similar faces of other furry mammals, such as a red panda, a bear and people.
mixed4b:443.CPS_s3: The unit responds to the faces of upright dogs and other canids, firing most strongly at the eye/upper-face region (eye, brow and cheek next to the muzzle). It responds more weakly to similar furry mammal faces such as a red panda or bear, and to faces in general, including a human face.
mixed4b:443.CPN_s1: The unit responds to upright, frontal canid faces, mostly dog faces. Its peak sits on the eye/muzzle region, and it extends weakly to faces of related canids such as foxes and wolves.
mixed4b:443.CPN_s2: The unit detects upright, front-facing canine faces (dogs, plus wolves and foxes). Its strongest response falls on the eye/forehead region, and it needs the eyes and muzzle laid out in their normal arrangement.
mixed4b:443.CPN_s3: The unit responds to upright, front-facing canine faces, peaking around the eye/muzzle region of dogs, and also fires on dog-like wild canids such as wolves and foxes.
mixed4b:443.CPSN_s1: Responds to the upright, roughly frontal face of a dog, peaking around the eye and upper muzzle region. It responds more weakly to similar canid-like faces such as foxes, wolves and red pandas, and only faintly to other faces such as a rooster, a person or a doll.
mixed4b:443.CPSN_s2: Responds to upright, front-facing canid faces (dogs, wolves, foxes), most strongly around the eye/cheek region of a dog's face seen from the front. It responds more weakly to other frontal furry mammal faces (red panda, bear) and faintly to human or doll faces.
mixed4b:443.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to the upright, front-facing face of a canid (dog, wolf, fox), peaking at the eye/upper-cheek region of a frontal dog face. It responds more weakly to other frontal mammal-like faces such as a red panda, a bear and a human cheek.

mixed4b:429.CP_s1: The unit responds to an upright, frontal dog face, peaking around the eye/muzzle region (eye, nose and snout together). Breed, coat colour and fur texture make little difference.
mixed4b:429.CP_s2: Responds to upright, frontal dog faces, peaking around the eye and muzzle region (the eye/nose arrangement of a dog's face) across many breeds and coat colours.
mixed4b:429.CP_s3: The unit responds to upright, frontal dog faces, peaking at the eye/muzzle region of a face seen roughly head-on, across many breeds, coat colours and fur textures.
mixed4b:429.CPS_s1: Responds to the upright frontal face of a dog, peaking around the eye and upper-muzzle region next to the eye, across many breeds. It responds more weakly to dog-like faces of other animals such as a cheetah, and barely to human faces.
mixed4b:429.CPS_s2: Responds to the eye region of upright, frontal dog faces, the area between the eye and the muzzle, across many breeds. It responds weakly to similar eye-and-face regions of other furry mammals such as a cheetah or a rabbit, and of humans.
mixed4b:429.CPS_s3: Responds to the upright face of a dog, centred on the eye and the area between the eyes and muzzle, across many breeds. It responds more weakly to similar upright animal faces (cheetah, bird head) and barely to human faces.
mixed4b:429.CPN_s1: The unit detects upright, front-facing dog faces, firing most strongly on the eye/muzzle region of a canine face seen from the front.
mixed4b:429.CPN_s2: The unit responds to an upright, frontal dog face (eyes above the muzzle, often small to medium terrier-like or fluffy breeds), with peak activity around the eye and muzzle region.
mixed4b:429.CPN_s3: The unit responds to upright, frontal dog faces, peaking on the eye/nose region of the face (particularly near an eye) across many breeds and coat colours.
mixed4b:429.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to upright, frontal dog faces, with the box most often on the eye/upper-muzzle region beside the nose. It responds more weakly to related animal faces such as a cheetah or fox and to human faces or hair.
mixed4b:429.CPSN_s2: Responds to upright, frontal dog faces, peaking on the eye region beside the muzzle, especially in small and medium fluffy or pointy-eared breeds. It responds more weakly to similar faces of other animals (cheetah, fox) and slightly to human faces.
mixed4b:429.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to upright, frontal dog faces, peaking on the region around the eye and muzzle of small and medium dogs such as terriers, corgis and toy breeds. It responds more weakly to similar faces of other mammals, such as a cheetah, a dingo and a rabbit, and only faintly to human faces.

mixed4d:409.CP_s1: The unit responds to the side-view profile of an upright, horizontally elongated body resting on supports, chiefly the torso of a standing dog or other quadruped seen from the side. It extends more weakly to cars and trucks seen side-on, whose body over wheels has a similar layout.
mixed4d:409.CP_s2: The unit responds to two unrelated things. One is the side-on torso of a standing dog or similar quadruped, seen upright in profile. The other is the side-on body and front-wheel area of a car or other road vehicle.
mixed4d:409.CP_s3: The unit responds to a side-profile view of an upright, horizontally elongated body raised on supports: the flank of a standing four-legged animal (mostly dogs, also a weasel) or the side of a car or truck above its wheels.
mixed4d:409.CPS_s1: The unit responds to the side-on, horizontally elongated body of an object standing on legs or wheels: mostly the torso of a standing dog seen in profile, and equally the body-and-wheel region of a car or van seen from the side.
mixed4d:409.CPS_s2: The unit responds to the torso of an upright four-legged animal seen from the side, mostly dogs. It also responds to the side or front-quarter body of cars and trucks, which have a similar shape: a horizontal body raised on legs or wheels.
mixed4d:409.CPS_s3: The unit responds to the side-view torso of upright four-legged animals, mostly dogs (also weasel, llama, warthog, lynx). Separately, it responds to the side or front-quarter body panels of cars and vans near a wheel.
mixed4d:409.CPN_s1: Responds to an upright, horizontally elongated body seen in side profile and resting on legs or wheels, mostly the flank of a standing dog (also a stoat) or the side of a car or truck.
mixed4d:409.CPN_s2: The unit responds to an upright, horizontally elongated body seen from the side and supported from below, such as a dog's or weasel's torso over its legs or a car's body over its wheels, with the peak on the mid-body or flank. It appears to encode this side-profile shape regardless of category, colour or texture.
mixed4d:409.CPN_s3: Responds to the flank of an upright, side-on, horizontally elongated body resting on supports below it, most often a standing four-legged animal (mostly dogs, also a weasel). It extends to the side profiles of cars and trucks, where the box falls on the body panel above the front wheel.
mixed4d:409.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to the mid-body of a horizontally elongated object seen upright in side profile, mainly standing dogs' torsos, and also cars and vans seen from the side (body panel over the wheels).
mixed4d:409.CPSN_s2: Responds to the side-on profile of a horizontally elongated body held up off the ground, chiefly the flank or torso of a standing quadruped (mostly dogs, also weasel, llama, warthog). It responds more weakly to the same lateral silhouette in road vehicles, such as the side of a car over its wheels.
mixed4d:409.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to the side-on body of a quadruped standing upright, mostly dogs and also weasel, llama and warthog, with the box on the torso above the legs. It extends to side views of cars and vans, the body panel just above the wheels, which is the same layout: a horizontal mass held up from below.

mixed4e:55.CP_s1: The unit responds to the muzzle and lower face of upright furry mammals, mainly cats, foxes, red pandas and lynxes, centred on the nose, whisker pad and mouth below the eyes. It responds more weakly to similar face regions on a hamster, a dog and a stork, plus one off-target car front grille.
mixed4e:55.CP_s2: Responds to the lower-central face of an upright furry mammal (muzzle, nose and mouth region of cats, foxes, red pandas, lynxes, hamsters and dogs), with weak spillover to similar face-like structures such as a stork's eye and beak base and a car's front grille.
mixed4e:55.CP_s3: Responds to the muzzle/snout region of upright furry mammal faces (cats, foxes, red pandas, lynx, hamster, dog), especially the nose-mouth area with whiskers and light fur below the eyes. It also responds weakly to similar face-like structures such as a stork's head and a car's front grille.
mixed4e:55.CPS_s1: The unit responds to the muzzle/snout region of furry mammal faces, centered just below and between the eyes around the nose and whisker pad, most strongly on foxes, red pandas and cats. It responds more weakly to other animal faces (dogs, hamsters, a meerkat, a monkey, a white stork head) and to a few car-front shapes.
mixed4e:55.CPS_s2: The unit responds to the lower-center face (muzzle, nose and whisker pad below the eyes) of furry mammals seen upright and roughly frontal, especially foxes, red pandas and cats, with weaker responses to dog, hamster, lynx and meerkat faces. It also fires weakly on similar curved white-and-dark structures such as a stork's face and a car's front grille.
mixed4e:55.CPS_s3: Responds to the lower-face/muzzle region of furry mammal faces, especially cats, foxes and red pandas: the area of nose, cheek and whiskers below the eyes, viewed upright. Weaker responses extend to dog, hamster, meerkat and monkey faces, plus occasional non-animal glossy curved shapes such as a car fender.
mixed4e:55.CPN_s1: Responds to the upright muzzle/snout region of small furry mammal faces, mainly cats, foxes, red pandas and lynxes: the nose-mouth area with white or light fur and whiskers just below the eyes. Weaker responses come from similar light-on-dark face patterns such as a hamster, a sheltie dog and a stork's white head, plus an odd car-grille hit.
mixed4e:55.CPN_s2: The unit responds to the muzzle and lower face (nose, mouth and whisker area) of upright, frontal furry animal faces, mainly cats, foxes, red pandas and lynxes, with weaker responses to similar faces of other animals such as a hamster, a dog and a stork's head.
mixed4e:55.CPN_s3: The unit responds to the upright snout/muzzle region of furry mammal faces, mainly cats, foxes and red pandas: the nose, mouth and whisker area seen roughly face-on. It also responds more weakly to similar face-like structures such as a stork's head and a car's front grille.
mixed4e:55.CPSN_s1: The unit responds to the face of a furry mammal, centred on the muzzle, nose and whisker area just below the eyes, seen upright and from the front (cats, foxes, red pandas, lynx, hamsters, dogs). It responds more weakly to similar small mammal faces such as meerkats, monkeys and ferrets, and to the white feathered face of a stork.
mixed4e:55.CPSN_s2: Responds to the muzzle/snout region of upright furry mammal faces (cats, foxes, red pandas, lynx, hamsters, dogs), especially the nose-and-whisker area just below and between the eyes, with weaker responses to similar face-like or fur-textured patterns.
mixed4e:55.CPSN_s3: The unit responds to the muzzle/cheek region of upright, front-facing furry mammal faces (foxes, red pandas, cats, hamsters, lynx), especially pale fur around the nose and whiskers just below the eyes. Weaker responses extend to dog faces and other animal or face-like regions, such as a stork's white head and a car's rounded front.

mixed5a:719.CP_s1: The unit appears to respond to curved, arc-shaped contours on close-up handmade or manufactured objects, such as rounded edges of mice, shoes, knee pads and stockings, and the collar or neckline curves in #5 and #9. It also responds, possibly as an extension, to ornamental radial or petal patterns made of repeated curved strokes (brooch, manhole cover, printed flowers, lily).
mixed5a:719.CP_s2: The unit mainly responds to curved, convex contours of compact man-made objects against a contrasting background, such as the edges of a mouse, shoes, stockings, knee pads, a teapot or a breastplate. It responds more weakly to ornamented or decorated surfaces made of curved shapes, such as brooch petals, crochet, a manhole-cover pattern, flowers and printed fabric.
mixed5a:719.CP_s3: The unit seems to respond to curved, rounded contours and ornamental motifs on close-up handmade or manufactured objects, such as curved object outlines (mouse, stocking, shoe, knee pad, teapot) and radial or floral decorative patterns (brooch, manhole cover, bib, basket, flower). mixed5a:719.CPS_s1: The unit seems to respond mainly to curved, rounded contours and edges on man-made, crafted objects, such as the rim of a mouse, an armour neckline, a stocking outline, a bow tie or a shoe toe.
